subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The EMF output of an AC generator with a coil rotating at constant speed is:
questions.explain: Uniform rotation produces a sinusoidally varying flux linkage, giving a sinusoidal alternating EMF.

questions.q: The half-life of capacitor discharge (time for charge to halve) is related to the time constant by:
questions.explain: t½ = ln2 × RC ≈ 0.69RC.

questions.q: Two planets have the same radius, but planet B has twice the mass of planet A. The escape velocity of B compared with A is:
questions.explain: Since v_esc ∝ √M for fixed R, doubling the mass multiplies escape velocity by √2.

questions.q: The gravitational field strength inside a hollow spherical shell of mass is:
questions.explain: The contributions from all parts of the shell cancel, giving zero field everywhere inside.

questions.q: On a graph of ln(Q) against time for a discharging capacitor, the gradient equals:
questions.explain: Taking logs of Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC) gives ln Q = ln Q₀ − t/RC, so the gradient is −1/RC.

questions.q: When a capacitor discharges through a resistor, the charge follows:
questions.explain: Discharge is exponential decay: Q = Q₀e^(−t/RC).

questions.q: The work done moving a mass along an equipotential surface is:
questions.explain: There is no change in potential along an equipotential, so no work is done.

questions.q: A satellite is moved to a higher orbit. Its orbital speed:
questions.explain: Since v = √(GM/r), a larger orbital radius means a smaller orbital speed.

questions.q: An ideal transformer has 100 turns on the primary and 500 turns on the secondary. If the primary voltage is 12 V, the secondary voltage is:
questions.explain: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p, so V_s = 12 × 500/100 = 60 V (a step-up transformer).

questions.q: Newton's law of gravitation states that the force between two point masses is proportional to:
options: the sum of the masses and inversely proportional to r²
the sum of the masses and inversely proportional to r
the product of the masses and inversely proportional to r²
the product of the masses and inversely proportional to r
questions.explain: F = GMm/r², so the force is proportional to the product of the masses and follows an inverse-square law with separation.

questions.q: For a sinusoidal AC supply, the rms voltage relates to the peak voltage by:
questions.explain: For a sinusoidal waveform, V_rms = V_peak/√2.

questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explain: With an inverse-square law, doubling r reduces the force by a factor of 2² = 4.

questions.q: A wire of length 0.20 m carries a current of 5.0 A perpendicular to a field of flux density 0.30 T. The force on it is:
Gravitational potential at a point is defined as:
options: the force per unit mass at that point
the work done to move a unit charge
the work done per unit mass to bring a mass from infinity to that point
the energy stored per unit volume
questions.explain: Gravitational potential V is the work done per unit mass in bringing a small test mass from infinity to the point.

questions.q: A coil of 200 turns encloses an area of 0.010 m² in a field of 0.50 T (normal to the coil). The flux linkage is:
questions.explain: Flux linkage NΦ = NBA = 200 × 0.50 × 0.010 = 1.0 Wb-turns.

questions.q: For a charged particle of mass m and charge q moving at speed v perpendicular to field B, the radius of its circular path is:
questions.explain: Setting Bqv = mv²/r gives r = mv/(Bq).

questions.q: Capacitance is defined as:
questions.explain: Capacitance C = Q/V, the charge stored per unit potential difference.

questions.q: A charged oil drop of charge q is held stationary between horizontal plates. The electric force on it equals:
questions.explain: For equilibrium the electric force qE balances the weight mg.

questions.q: The magnetic flux density B has the SI unit:
questions.explain: Magnetic flux density is measured in tesla; 1 T = 1 Wb m⁻².

questions.q: Near the Earth's surface a uniform gravitational field is assumed. Its field lines are:
questions.explain: Over small regions the field is approximately uniform, shown by parallel, equally spaced, vertical lines.

questions.q: Escape velocity from a planet's surface is given by:
questions.explain: Equating kinetic energy to the magnitude of potential energy gives v_esc = √(2GM/R).

questions.q: The unit V m⁻¹ for electric field strength is equivalent to:
questions.explain: V m⁻¹ = (J C⁻¹)/m = N C⁻¹, since J = N m.

questions.q: The gravitational potential energy of a mass m at potential V is:
questions.explain: Potential energy E = mV = −GMm/r for a mass m in the field.

questions.q: A 2.0 µF capacitor discharges through a 1.0 MΩ resistor. The time constant is:
For a circular orbit, the centripetal acceleration equals:
options: the gravitational field strength at that radius
questions.explain: Gravity provides the centripetal force, so a = v²/r = GM/r² = g at that radius.

questions.q: The electric field between two parallel plates a distance d apart with potential difference V is:
questions.explain: For a uniform field between plates, E = V/d.

questions.q: To increase the time constant of an RC discharge circuit, you could:
questions.explain: Since τ = RC, increasing either resistance or capacitance increases the time constant.

questions.q: The National Grid transmits power at very high voltage mainly to:
options: reduce the current for a given power, lowering I²R heating losses in the cables
increase the current and so the power delivered
increase the resistance of the cables
questions.explain: For a given power, higher voltage means lower current, and since power loss in cables is I²R, lower current greatly reduces resistive heating losses.

questions.q: The unit of gravitational field strength N kg⁻¹ is equivalent to:
questions.explain: N kg⁻¹ = (kg m s⁻²)/kg = m s⁻², the same as acceleration.
